concept.name: Substrate substitution
concept.description: Change the physical carrier that performs the operation instead of optimising the existing carrier further.

why_interesting: The problem's 'Computing Model' dimension (what kind of computation the system performs and how) is where the conventional approach carries a structural assumption: The dominant computing model is uniform and synchronous, so it spends energy on operations whose result the application does not actually need. AARL took a mechanism that already works in photonics, neuromorphic engineering, analog computing, condensed matter physics - Change the physical carrier that performs the operation instead of optimising the existing carrier further. - and asked what happens if it is applied to GPU. If the mechanism transfers, the gain would come from removing that assumption rather than from tuning the existing design. Whether it transfers is exactly what is not established here.

first_experiment.objective: Establish whether the mechanism moves achievable operations per second for GPU at all, before tuning anything.
first_experiment.design: Baseline A: the conventional computing model approach. Variant B: the Substrate substitution mechanism applied only to the compute model dimension. Keep every other parameter identical and use the same seed/warm-up.
first_experiment.decision_rule: Only claim support if B moves achievable operations per second outside the run-to-run spread of A; if the spread is larger than the effect, report INCONCLUSIVE rather than a direction.
first_experiment.what_would_make_it_stop: If A is already at the physical or structural limit of achievable operations per second, the comparison cannot discriminate and the design must change.
